message.content: Pizza’s roots trace back to ancient civilizations—flatbreads were common across the Mediterranean—but the dish we recognize today began taking shape in **Naples, Italy** during the late 18th‑early 19th centuries. Neapolitan cooks started topping their thin crusts with fresh tomatoes (a relatively new crop at the time), olive oil, garlic, oregano, and mozzarella cheese. By the mid‑1800s, this “pizza” had become popular among working‑class locals and eventually spread beyond Naples, evolving into countless regional variations around the world.
